summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, was admitted for symptomatic in-stent restenosis of the renal artery to his transplanted kidney. He presented with elevated blood pressure, and prior ultrasound showed increased renal artery velocities. He underwent elective balloon angioplasty of the stenotic segment without complications. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with no change in kidney function. His pain was controlled, and he tolerated diet advancement. He was discharged home on day two with continued immunosuppressive, antihypertensive, and dual antiplatelet therapy, and instructions to follow up with vascular surgery in two weeks.
